clue.text: Diagram showing figures from local church paintings

parts.note: a local is a British pub, so a bar
paintings collectively are art

explanation.surface: Someone sketches numbers taken from the pictures in a parish church.
explanation.definitionFit: A chart of bars is a graph that displays numerical figures visually.

clue.text: Courts held outside America, in part of Europe

indicators.note: held outside means the courts are put round the abbreviation for America

parts.note: atria are open central courts of buildings

explanation.surface: Tennis courts somewhere in Europe are surrounded by Americans.
explanation.definitionFit: This Alpine republic with Vienna as its capital is a country in central Europe.

clue.text: Kind of furniture slightly damaged, broken by new porter

indicators.note: broken by means the word for slightly damaged is split open by the letter for new

parts.note: chipped means slightly damaged, as crockery is
porter is a dark beer, so a kind of ale

explanation.surface: A removal porter has knocked and chipped a piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Furniture in the style of the eighteenth-century cabinetmaker Thomas Chippendale is a recognised kind.

clue.text: In suitable form, new play appears outside West End

indicators.note: appears outside means the rearranged play surrounds the following letter
new signals that the letters of play are made into a new arrangement
End picks the last letter of the word West

explanation.surface: A new play suitably opens away from London's theatre district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West End', London's theatre district, is split: End takes the final letter of West, T.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something aptly means doing it in a fitting, suitable manner.

clue.text: Not a good subject in portrait, originally

indicators.note: in tells us the letters run inside the words portrait, originally

explanation.surface: In the original painting the sitter was a poor subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'subject' looks artistic, but it means a subject of the crown: one who betrays it is no good.
explanation.definitionFit: A disloyal subject who betrays their monarch or country is the opposite of a good one.

clue.text: In class, a learner is conventionally correct

parts.note: a form is a school class in Britain
L is the learner driver's plate abbreviation

explanation.surface: A pupil in a school class behaves with proper decorum.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal behaviour follows established convention and etiquette exactly.

clue.text: Company installing genuine article as safety device

indicators.note: installing means the company word takes the following pieces inside it

parts.note: a firm is a business company
real means genuine
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A firm fits a real piece of safety equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell or siren warning of fire is a device for protecting people's safety.

clue.text: A single journey

definitions.meaning: in cricket, one ... scored between the wickets is a single
a trip or regular route, as a bus makes

explanation.definitionFit: A single in cricket counts one run, and a short trip is also called a run.

clue.text: Lacking introductory letter, unpaid for very long time

indicators.note: lacking introductory letter means the first letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: wageless means working without pay

explanation.surface: An unpaid worker has gone without letters of introduction for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ageless lasts for an immensely long time, seeming eternal.

clue.text: Unusually clean waters in North American river

indicators.note: unusually signals that the letters of the following words are set out in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Strangely unpolluted water flows in a large river in North America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word but its letters are part of the fodder: CLEAN WATERS IN gives exactly thirteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This waterway drains the Great Lakes into the Atlantic, a major river of Canada and the USA.

clue.text: Decline in vigour without a leading award

indicators.note: without a leading tells us to remove the letter A from the front of the word

parts.note: atrophy is a wasting away or decline in strength

explanation.surface: An athlete past their best fails to win a top prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup or shield given to a winner is a prize, an award.

clue.text: Made kind of roof that's reduced temperature and shaded

indicators.note: reduced means the word temperature is cut down to its initial letter, its abbreviation

parts.note: in drawing, to shade is to hatch with fine lines

explanation.surface: A roofer explains a roof that lowered the heat and gave shade.
explanation.definitionFit: To thatch is to make a roof of straw or reeds, so a thatched roof was made that way.

clue.text: King joining Mary's devoted follower, her brother

parts.note: Charles is the name of several English kings
in the nursery rhyme, Mary's little lamb followed her everywhere

explanation.surface: A king teams up with the nursery rhyme lamb, Mary's sibling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'her' refers to Mary: Mary Lamb wrote Tales from Shakespeare with her brother, the essayist.
explanation.definitionFit: The essayist who wrote under the name Elia was brother to the writer Mary Lamb.

clue.text: Strange anagram at start of clue for "historic document"

indicators.note: strange signals that the following letters are to be rearranged oddly
start of points to the opening letter of the word clue

explanation.surface: A setter describes an odd anagram used to begin a clue for a famous charter.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is self-referential: ANAGRAM, AT and C from 'start of clue' are shuffled together.
explanation.definitionFit: The great charter sealed by King John in 1215 is a celebrated historic document.

clue.text: University clubs in morning game

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
AM is short for ante meridiem, the morning
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: Student societies play cards before noon.
explanation.definitionFit: This ancient English seat of learning on the river Cam is a famous university.

clue.text: Primate set over southern part of church

indicators.note: set over means the primate is placed around the following letter

parts.note: an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: A monkey is perched above the south end of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: The rounded or vaulted recess at the east end of a church is this architectural part.

clue.text: Part of British Isles linked to a part of United States

parts.note: IOW abbreviates the Isle of Wight, an island off southern England

explanation.surface: An island in Britain is twinned with somewhere in America.
explanation.definitionFit: This Midwestern state is one of the fifty that make up the USA.

clue.text: Supervised part of test with tool

parts.note: in cricket a Test match is divided into overs of six balls
a saw is a cutting tool

explanation.surface: Someone oversees an exam stage using a piece of equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee work is to supervise it, so oversaw means supervised.

clue.text: Note an inclination in modern kind of composer

parts.note: a minim is a musical note, the half note
an gives the letter A, the indefinite article
a list is a lean or tilt, as of a ship

explanation.surface: A music critic observes a tendency in a contemporary composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Minimalism is a modern school of composition, so a composer such as Steve Reich is one of this kind.

clue.text: Token change on main line

indicators.note: change signals that the letters of on main are altered in order

explanation.surface: A small switch is made on a mainline railway.
explanation.definitionFit: A token payment is a nominal one, small and symbolic only.

clue.text: Feeble son supported by uncle, perhaps

indicators.note: supported by in a down clue places the son letter above the lender

parts.note: uncle is old British slang for a pawnbroker, one kind of lender

explanation.surface: A weak son depends on an uncle for money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncle' is slang for a pawnbroker, who lends money against pledged goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A slender chance or argument is weak and feeble.

clue.text: Message from member, ringleader in gang

indicators.note: in means the following pieces are put inside the word for gang

parts.note: a team is a group or gang
a leg is a limb, a member of the body
the leader of the word ring is its first letter

explanation.surface: A gang member receives a note from the head of the gang.
explanation.definitionFit: A telegram is a message sent by telegraph, delivered as a printed slip.

clue.text: Tree on river looking more healthy

indicators.note: on in an across clue places the tree after the river letter

parts.note: an osier is a willow tree

explanation.surface: A tree by the water looks in better condition than before.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosy cheeks suggest good health, so rosier means looking healthier.

clue.text: Clothes I had starched too much

parts.note: a rig or rig-out is an outfit of clothes
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone admits their outfit was over-starched.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric starched too heavily becomes stiff and unbending.

clue.text: Position taken by railway worker on watch

parts.note: standing is a position or rank
a guard is a member of a train's crew

explanation.surface: A railwayman takes up a post while keeping a lookout.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone standing guard is keeping watch over something as a sentry does.

clue.text: Bill successfully prosecuted in a court

explanation.surface: A case against a bill succeeds in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prosecuted' means carried through, not taken to law: a bill pushed through parliament becomes law.
explanation.definitionFit: A parliamentary bill that has passed all its stages becomes a statute, an Act.

clue.text: Wheat's arranged in row after reaping

indicators.note: arranged signals that the letters of the preceding word are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A farmer lays out cut wheat in lines in the field.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the 's stands for 'is' in the surface but its S is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A swathe is the strip of cut grain left lying after a scythe or reaper passes.

clue.text: Beetle spotted by black hen?

definitions.meaning: a small red beetle marked with black spots
a hen is a female bird, playfully a lady among birds

explanation.definitionFit: The red beetle with black spots is this insect, and a female bird could be called a lady bird.
